defects.claim_says: later_events lists only EO 12553; the earlier-end check and the OFR reconciliation never mention EO 11636, and the reason treats Section 4's conforming change to subsection (d) of Section 21 of EO 11264 as continuing unchanged until 1982-05-21
defects.source_says: EO 11636 of December 17, 1971 (36 FR 24901; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11636.txt), Sec. 18(b), further amends Section 21 of EO 11264 'as amended': (1) 'by revising subsection (d) to read as follows', replacing the subsection (d) that EO 11434 Sec. 4(c) had conformed, and (2) by adding a new subsection (f) governing designation of members under subsection (b)(3), the paragraph EO 11434 Sec. 4(b) added. The order became effective on publication (FR of December 24, 1971). Under owner ruling 2026-10-21-strike-and-insert.md such a restatement is a later_event recording the text before and after; the packet dossier chain lists this EO 11636 amendment of Section 21 as a lead, and the claim leaves it unaddressed.

packet dossier EO:11434 chain (includes EO:11636 amend Section 21), missing, conflicts (FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT for EO 12363)
reasoning: Identity, text and inventory are sound, and the ending analysis is correct: EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) expressly revoked Sections 1, 3 and 5 effective as of 1981-02-15 (Sec. 11); Sections 2 and 4 operate on EO 11264 Part II, which EO 12292 left in force (Sec. 10(h) reached only Part III), and they ended when EO 12363 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11264 as amended on 1982-05-21, the latest clause end and the whole-order end; EO 12553 of 1986 is a later formal disposition; every held OFR note (Amended by EO 12107; Revoked in part by EO 12292 and by EO 12363; Revoked by EO 12553) is reconciled; no savings clause applies. The claim is rejected because it omits EO 11636 Sec. 18(b) (1971), which restated subsection (d) of Section 21 of EO 11264, the text Section 4(c) of this order had conformed, and added subsection (f) governing the (b)(3) members that Section 4(b) created. The strike-and-insert ruling requires that amendment as a later event with before-and-after text, and the claim's earlier-end check does not address the dossier chain lead naming it. The end dates do not change. Notes (not defects): two quotations in the reasons differ from the held OCR bytes in spacing only ('November 8,1968;' where EO 12292 Sec. 10(i) reads 'November 8, 1968;', and 'Executive Order No. 11264' where the EO 12363 OCR reads 'Executive O rder No. 11264'); a corrected claim should copy the held bytes exactly.

defects.source_says: EO 13332 Sec. 8 ('Executive Order 13322 of December 30, 2003, is superseded.') is signed 'March 3, 2004' (69 FR 10891, Federal Register of March 8, 2004); the cited source's signing_date is 2004-03-03 and the OFR note reads 'Superseded by: EO 13332, March 3, 2004'. A 2001-03-03 end also precedes EO 13322's own signing on December 30, 2003. The claim's own judgment reasons and research rationale state 2004-03-03, so the date fields contradict both the source and the claim's reasons.

packet dossier EO:13322 chain (EO 13332 only), machine searches (USC 1, eCFR 0, OFR 2)
reasoning: Identity and inventory are sound: EO 13322 of December 30, 2003 (69 FR 231) is the 2004 pay-adjustment order, and the 16 clauses cover Sec. 1 to 8 and every subsection. Its only ending instrument is EO 13332 Sec. 8, signed March 3, 2004, with no separate effective date; the reasons correctly use 2004-03-03 and disclose the January 2004 schedule dates as an alternative. Every structured end date, however, reads 2001-03-03, which matches no source and falls before the order itself was signed. The claim is rejected for the wrong date and for the conflict between its date fields and its own reasons.
